input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view in the Dashboard (side-by-side and diff)

## Description

Deliver a run comparison view in the Dashboard: users select two or more
training and pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side,
including a diff presentation that highlights which parameters and metrics
changed between two selected runs. This gives data scientists in-platform
visibility into what changed between candidate runs, replacing the current
export-to-spreadsheet workflow that model promotion decisions rely on.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs from the runs list in the Dashboard.
- Comparison view rendering parameters and metrics for all selected runs side
  by side, using the same run data already surfaced on the per-run pages.
- Diff mode for two selected runs: highlight which parameters and metrics
  changed between them.
- Support for both training runs and pipeline runs, including runs executed
  via Data Science Pipelines.
- Respect the strategy's out-of-scope boundaries: no automatic best-run
  selection or promotion, and no comparison across clusters or across
  projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can select two or more runs from the runs list and open the
  comparison view showing those runs' parameters and metrics side by side.
- Given two selected runs, the comparison view highlights which parameters and
  metrics changed between them (diff presentation).
- Comparison works for training runs and for pipeline runs executed via Data
  Science Pipelines, with parameters and metrics consistent with what the
  per-run pages show (passive-component validation for Data Science
  Pipelines).
- Comparison is scoped within a single project; no cross-cluster or
  cross-project comparison is offered.
- No automatic best-run selection or promotion behavior is introduced.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): select two or more runs and view parameters and metrics side by
  side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1): run diff view highlighting which parameters and metrics changed
  between two selected runs — consolidated with HLR-1 as one capability; the
  diff view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the
  same run data, so it is covered by this epic rather than split out.

# Link registered model versions to producing runs

## Description

Record, on each registered model version in the Model Registry, a link back to
the training or pipeline run that produced it, using the registry's existing
metadata extension point on model versions. This makes the producing run
programmatically resolvable so a run comparison can later be opened from the
Model Registry.

## Scope

- Model version metadata carries a reference to the run that produced it (run
  type and run identifier), via the Model Registry's custom-properties
  extension point on ModelVersion entities.
- The link is settable and readable through the Model Registry REST API so
  that registration tooling can record it and consumers can resolve the
  originating run of any model version.
- Applies uniformly to runs from training jobs and from Data Science
  Pipelines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A registered model version can carry a reference to the run that produced
  it, set and read through the Model Registry REST API (custom-properties
  extension point on ModelVersion).
- The reference distinguishes run type (training run vs pipeline run) and
  identifies the run sufficiently for a consumer to retrieve its parameters
  and metrics.
- Model versions without a producing-run link remain fully functional (the
  link is optional metadata).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, registry side): registered model versions link back to the run
  that produced them.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry UI

## Description

Add an entry point in the Dashboard's Model Registry UI so a user can open a
run comparison starting from a registered model version, using the
producing-run link recorded on that model version. This closes the loop from
model promotion context back to run evidence: a data scientist reviewing a
registered model version can jump straight into a comparison of the run that
produced it.

## Scope

- Entry point in the Model Registry UI within the Dashboard (model version
  detail view) that opens the run comparison view populated with the run
  linked as the producing run of that model version.
- Ability to add further runs to the comparison once opened, using the same
  selection behavior as the runs-list entry path.
- Graceful handling of model versions that carry no producing-run link (entry
  point hidden or disabled).

## Acceptance Criteria

- From a registered model version that carries a producing-run link, a user
  can open the run comparison view with that run included in the comparison.
- The entry point resolves both training-run and pipeline-run links.
- Further runs can be added to the comparison after opening it from the
  registry.
- Model versions without a producing-run link show no broken entry point
  (hidden or disabled with no error).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, Dashboard side): a comparison can be opened from the Model
  Registry.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

Author user documentation for the run comparison workflow, covering both
starting points: comparing runs from the runs list, and opening a comparison
from the Model Registry via a registered model version's producing-run link.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Comparing runs from the runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the
  side-by-side parameter and metric view, and using the diff presentation for
  two selected runs.
- Opening a comparison from the Model Registry: navigating from a registered
  model version to the comparison of its producing run, and adding further
  runs to that comparison.
- Coverage of both training runs and pipeline runs in the comparison workflow,
  including runs executed via Data Science Pipelines.
- Statement of boundaries: comparison is within a single project; no
  cross-cluster or cross-project comparison; no automatic best-run selection
  or promotion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the
  runs list (multi-select, side-by-side view, diff for two runs).
- Published documentation covers opening a comparison from the Model Registry
  (model version to producing-run comparison, adding runs).
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of
  the comparison view, the model-version run link, and the registry entry
  point, and passes that review.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs
  list and the registry.

Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs.

## Triage

Not below-threshold: the strategy spans multiple components (Dashboard, Model
Registry, Data Science Pipelines), multiple owning teams, and distinct work
